objective: Distinguish includes membership from indexOf position, especially for NaN, without mutating opaque values.

relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Membership and first position are useful distinct queries.
relevanceRationale.transferable: SameValueZero versus strict equality is transferable.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The foundation task should teach the difference explicitly.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: NaN exposes two incorrect supplied solutions and a false explanation.

defects: The prompt falsely said both methods compare strictly.
Junior manual strict search and senior index-derived membership disagreed with includes for NaN.
Both boards skipped at least one of the requested methods.
rationale: Explain SameValueZero for includes and strict equality for indexOf: [NaN] yields present true with index -1. Make junior and senior call both methods rather than deriving membership from index. Define bounded dense read-only opaque arrays, original object identity, zero-sign equality and fresh result objects. Add NaN, distinct equal-looking object references, undefined, signed zero and10000positions. Preserve type noncoercion and first-occurrence rules.

objective: Reduce a read-only finite Number list to its unrounded largest value with explicit empty handling.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: reduce and maximum accumulation remain current.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Handling negative-only and empty data is practical.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Accumulator seeds, nonmutation and numeric boundaries are transferable.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The foundation task deliberately practices reduce.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Fractional and large immutable inputs reject rounding and sorting shortcuts.

defects: Finite numeric bounds, no-rounding and read-only ownership were implicit.
Rounding maxima and sorting the source passed old probes.
Tie behavior for the two zero signs was unspecified across Math.max versus first-best forms.
rationale: Retain all correct reduce boards and explicitly allow either sign of equal zero, avoiding a false discrepancy with Math.max. Specify bounded finite signed Numbers, frozen/read-only dense arrays, no sorting/rounding and null before reducing empty input. Add1.005, direct source-order observation, zero equality and10000negative values with a tiny late maximum. The junior processes its seeded first value twice without changing finite numeric correctness or linear complexity; no unnecessary rewrite is made.
